newsitem.title: CANADA: CanWest names Peter Viner as CEO.
newsitem.headline: CanWest names Peter Viner as CEO.

text.p: CanWest Global Communications Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Israel Asper said on Monday that the company appointed Peter Viner as president and chief executive, effective immediately.
Asper added that he would remain as chairman of the Winnipeg-based television broadcaster.
Viner headed CanWest Global's Australian operations and was previously chief executive of Australia's Network Ten.
Asper said he would remain involved in CanWest operations, with focus on the company's external growth and development.

He said the decision to hand the top management post to Viner instead of one of his three children, who all hold senior management positions at CanWest, was made because it was "too early" for the children to move up.

"What we're doing today has the full enthusiastic support of the children. And it in no way forecloses their future roles, should they choose, to want roles in management. But they will have to earn that. They will not inherit it," Asper told a news conference.
"Nor should Peter be viewed as an interim...as anything but the boss," Asper added.
He said he would act as an adviser during the transition period and hoped shortly to "promote himself out of a job" and pursue a different career.
"I think I have the discipline not to haunt the halls of the place where a new chief executive is spreading his or her wings...the transistion period, I expect, will not be a long one," Asper said.
Viner, who joined CanWest in 1974, said he would focus on further growth in Canada and internationally.

"I feel the key for ongoing success at CanWest will be to continue recognizing value where it is not so obvious to others, and to back our judgment with the necessary resources. We have a proven business formula for success that can and has traveled successfully, and we recognize that our opportunities are worldwide," Viner said.

Asper said several development projects were in the works and should be completed by the end of the year, including the relaunching of CanWest's Quebec City television station into the Montreal market and a new television operation in Ireland.
CanWest in June made its first significant acquisition in commercial radio when it bought More FM, New Zealand's top- rated commercial radio network.
